entries.note: scripts/probe-surface.mjs, scripts/lint-shell.mjs and scripts/coverage-scripts.mjs share an ES-module import header plus the one-line repo-root computation. Reviewed and classified rather than removed, because removing it made things worse by this gate's own measure: extracting repoRootFrom() into scripts/lib/ and converting all ten call sites turned one family into three, since every rewritten header then carried the same extra import. It also broke the install-git-hooks scratch-clone test, which needs that script self-contained. Import statements are not extractable; this is portable boilerplate. The id moved from 7c84b6f6556d6b49 on 2026-08-08 when coverage-scripts.mjs became the third member: the fingerprint is over the family, so gaining a member re-keys it, and the classification is re-stated rather than inherited.

test/contract/repo-gates.test.mjs runs scripts/install-git-hooks.mjs against a throwaway clone twice, checking the hooksPath after each. The repetition IS the assertion — 'an installed clone stays installed', which is the idempotence claim the second run exists to make — so factoring it into a helper would delete the property under test and leave one call. Pre-existing and untouched; it re-keyed on 2026-08-08 only because the coverage slice changed content inside the same detected member span.

test/contract/worker-gateway-handoff-archive.test.mjs. Both families are the table-driven refusal shape itself: clone the reviewed lock or inject a dependency, perturb one field, expect a coded refusal. Introduced as detectable on 2026-08-08 when deleting the dead resolveLockedGatewayHandoffArchive wrapper repointed twelve call sites at the longer consumeLockedGatewayHandoffArchiveSync, which biome then reflowed onto multiple lines. Removal was attempted twice before classifying: first a single refuses() helper, which traded these two families for two others, then refusesMutatedLock() plus refuses(), which collapsed every hand-written frame and left only the per-case mutation at the call site. What remains is the shape two sibling tests share by design. Collapsing further means merging them into one parametrized test, trading two named refusals with two distinct reasons - the Protocol binding and the Sigstore identity - for one opaque one. Not worth it: a named failing test is the output this suite exists to produce.

note: Reviewed fixable-duplication overlay (item 5). Keyed by family identity (code: offset/path-independent content fingerprint; doc: family_signature). Stores only explicitly-classified families; an unlisted family defaults to 'unreviewed'. fixable_ceiling (count of 'fixable') is one-way and only decreases via a deliberate re-review. nose-baseline.json / doc-nose-baseline.json own drift detection; this overlay owns fixable classification.
